content:
Apple TV's current lineup of shows is quite strong, led by hit series such as "Slow Horses," "Ted Lasso," "Dark Matter," and the brand new comedy "Brothers" starring Matthew McConaughey. But there's plenty more excitement to come. Below is a roundup of everything new coming to Apple TV in October.

The Last First: Winter K2

  • Release date: October 2
  • Format: Film
  • Category: Documentary

Directed by Amir Bar-Lev, "The Last First: Winter K2" tells an intricate, thrilling, yet deeply moving story, examining the extreme mountaineering industry and its continually evolving culture. The film focuses on a 2021 expedition in which Icelandic mountaineer John Snorri Sigurjónsson, teamed with a Pakistani father-and-son duo Ali and Sajid Sadpara, set out to become the first people to summit K2 in winter conditions. Along the way, they encounter influencer mountaineers with their camera crews, paying clients on commercial expeditions, and legendary Nepalese mountaineer Nims and his team of Sherpas. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers to the icy summit of K2, through unpredictable weather, to reveal an unexpected, layered story — one woven with strategy and determination, class and status, money and power — all unfolding in a life-or-death environment.

The Sisters Grimm (Season 2)

  • Release date: October 2
  • Format: Series
  • Category: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters navigate a town full of fairy-tale and fantasy characters, dealing with heroes and villains while also investigating the disappearance of their parents. "The Sisters Grimm" blends exploration, fantasy and adventure, offering meaningful takeaways for audiences of all ages.

Small Prophets

  • Release date: October 7
  • Format: Series
  • Category: Comedy

"Small Prophets" is a comedy centered on eccentric Michael Sleep (played by Pearce Quigley). Since his beloved Clea disappeared seven years ago, he has been living a quiet life — working at a hardware store, visiting his father Brian (played by Sir Michael Palin), and hoping for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares an ancient recipe with him, with ingredients including rainwater, horse manure and a dash of alchemy. Skeptical but hopeful, Michael sets about making homunculi — magical tiny creatures that can predict the future — hoping to answer his most pressing question: "Will I ever see Clea again?"

Matchbox The Movie

  • Release date: October 9
  • Format: Film
  • Category: Action

Adapted from the classic Mattel toy, "Matchbox The Movie" is a thrilling, globe-trotting adventure about a group of friends who have known each other since childhood. Their lives are going on as usual until CIA undercover agent Sean (played by John Cena) — their long-lost former leader — returns to their small town, and they are inadvertently thrust into a thrilling, world-saving mission.

Tenzing

  • Release date: October 16
  • Format: Film
  • Category: Drama

"Tenzing" is based on a true story, recounting the lesser-known life of Tenzing Norgay (played by Genden Phuntsok). A gifted Himalayan mountaineer, he later teamed up with New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary (played by Tom Hiddleston) to become one of the first people to successfully summit Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (played by Thinley Lhamo) and supported by expedition secretary Jill Henderson (played by Caitríona Balfe), the two successfully convinced Colonel John Hunt (played by Willem Dafoe) to let Tenzing join the British expedition as a team member rather than a porter. Western climbers saw "Everest" as a peak waiting to be conquered, while Tenzing revered "Chomolungma" as a sacred mountain deity. The journey that followed was full of tensions of background, class and ambition, as well as the dangers of the mountain itself. But high above the world, empire, status and ambition gradually faded away, leaving only two outsiders who respected and trusted each other — for Tenzing, this was also the realization of his lifelong dream and spiritual mission.

Where's Wanda? (Season 2)

  • Release date: October 21
  • Format: Series
  • Category: Black comedy

Apple TV's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a black comedy about married couple Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, who are desperately searching for their 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who suddenly disappeared months earlier. After the police investigation hits a dead end, the family decides to take matters into their own hands, bringing in tech-savvy younger son Ole and getting hold of a batch of surveillance equipment. Posing as utility company workers, they install listening devices throughout the neighborhood and surrounding suburbs — only to discover that the neighbors behind closed doors are nothing like they appear.

Nocturne

  • Release date: October 30
  • Format: Series
  • Category: Crime drama

The series tells the story of Jonah Lynn (played by Liev Schreiber). A military veteran turned homicide detective, he has spent years on the streets of Philadelphia and grown weary, so he moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania in search of a quieter life. But when the town and his family are threatened by cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (played by [Graham — actor name retained as actor first name not clearly specified]), Jonah must fight to protect everything. As the hunt for Jurek's final victim reaches a critical stage, Jonah calls on his goddaughter, FBA agent Saga Bauer (played by [Beetz — actress first name not clearly specified]), to confront Jurek head-on — just how far will Jonah go?

New episodes: "Slow Horses," "Brothers" and more

Apple TV will also release new episodes of several currently airing series in October, including:

  • "Ted Lasso": Jason Sudeikis-starring comedy, with new episodes airing through October 7
  • "Last Seen": crime thriller, with new episodes airing through October 7
  • "Slow Horses": acclaimed British spy drama, with new episodes airing through October 21
  • "Dark Matter": sci-fi drama starring Joel Edgerton, with new episodes airing through October 30
  • "Brothers": comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, with new episodes airing through November 4

Of these new Apple TV titles for October, which ones are you planning to watch? Feel free to share in the comments.

Apple TV's monthly subscription is US$14.99, and you can enjoy additional discounts by subscribing through the Apple One bundle.
